newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends flat despite small U.S. recovery.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends flat despite small U.S. recovery.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

* NZ mid bonds claw back some ground from open
* Rest of curve stable, volumes thin
* Market awaits Thursday's inflation-linked bond tender
New Zealand debt ended steady on Wednesday after an uneventful session.
The mid bonds clawed back three basis points from their opening levels but, at their 7.96 percent finish, were still three basis points above Tuesday's close.
In the money market, 90-day bank bills ended on their 7.85 percent open, while the June bank bill futures contract was three basis points weaker at 92.05 with 2,025 contracts traded.

Dealers said the market tried to weaken in early trade on rumours of an offshore party unloading a dollar bloc portfolio, but flows were "pathetic" and the move was nipped in the bud by a lack of interest.
The market basically ignored the small rally staged by U.S. Treasuries, the stability of the Australian debt market and a recovery in the currency's Trade-Weighted Index to 68.41 from its 68.17 open.

It was equally dismissive of Reserve Bank governor Don Brash's latest repetition of his belief in a lower currency and higher interest rates. One dealer said he thought it was time the governor "stopped crying wolf".

"The TWI was weaker this morning, which tainted the short end, but it's come back okay this afternoon...I'm not quite sure why we didn't improve on the day on both ends of the curve really," another Wellington dealer said.
"There has been a bit of swap interest out in the two year part of the curve today, so that's probably generated a bit of weakness in those earlier bonds," he said.
Government bond tender details and a NZ$50 million tender of February 2016 inflation-indexed bonds, both due on Thursday, are the next items of interest on the local agenda.
